canonical.User-facing Definition: Temperature of seawater measured in situ at the observation's stated vertical level. This is a water-column quantity and should be used with depth or pressure metadata.
Temperature assigned to the ocean surface or near-surface layer. The exact physical layer depends on the observing method; preserve the SST subtype or measurement depth whenever it is known.
Temperature of the conductive skin layer at the air-sea interface, approximately the upper tens of micrometres and typically measured by infrared radiometry.
Temperature at the base of the conductive laminar sub-layer immediately below the ocean skin; microwave radiometers approximately sense this layer.
Near-surface temperature representative of water below the diurnal warm layer and therefore minimally affected by the daily surface heating cycle.
Temperature a seawater parcel would have after being moved adiabatically to a specified reference pressure, usually the sea surface.
TEOS-10 temperature variable designed to represent seawater heat content more accurately than potential temperature.
Practical Salinity Scale 1978 (PSS-78) salinity derived from conductivity ratio; dimensionless although often displayed as PSU.
TEOS-10 mass fraction of dissolved material in seawater, expressed as grams of solute per kilogram of seawater.
Salinity of the ocean's near-surface layer. Preserve whether it is in-situ practical salinity or a satellite retrieval and its effective sampling depth.
canonical.Required Qualifiers: salinity scale; retrieval type; measurement depth

canonical.User-facing Definition: Pressure exerted by seawater at the observation level, normally reported relative to atmospheric pressure. Ocean profiles commonly use decibars.
Vertical distance of the observation below the sea surface. It describes where the sample or measurement was taken, not the bottom depth.
Vertical distance from the sea surface or reference datum to the seafloor at the observation location.
Depth to the seafloor measured by a sounding system such as single-beam, multibeam, or crowdsourced echo sounding.
Electrical conductivity of seawater, used with temperature and pressure to derive practical salinity.
Mass per unit volume of seawater at the observed temperature, salinity, and pressure.
Density a seawater parcel would have if moved adiabatically to a specified reference pressure.
Measure of water cloudiness or light scattering caused by suspended particles; values depend strongly on the instrument and calibration.
Loss of a collimated light beam through water due to absorption and scattering. May be reported as beam attenuation coefficient or transmissivity.
Eastward component of seawater velocity; positive values indicate motion toward the east.
Northward component of seawater velocity; positive values indicate motion toward the north.
Magnitude of the horizontal seawater velocity vector at the stated depth.
Direction toward which the ocean current is flowing, measured clockwise from true north unless the source states otherwise.
Magnitude of horizontal wind velocity. Preserve measurement height or whether the value has been converted to an equivalent 10-m neutral wind.
Direction from which the wind is blowing, measured clockwise from true north.
Peak short-duration wind speed observed during the reporting interval.
Atmospheric pressure reduced to mean sea level or a barometric pressure observation used as the marine surface pressure measurement.
Temperature of the air at the sensor height above the ocean or platform.
Temperature to which air must be cooled at constant pressure for water vapour to reach saturation.
Ratio of actual water-vapour content to the amount needed for saturation at the same temperature, expressed as a percentage.
Horizontal distance at which an object can be seen and identified under prevailing atmospheric conditions.
Fraction of the sky covered by cloud. Historical marine reports may use coded tenths or oktas rather than a continuous fraction.
Liquid-equivalent water deposited from the atmosphere over an accumulation interval.
Solar shortwave radiant energy flux at the surface; preserve whether it is downward, upward, or net.
Thermal infrared radiant energy flux at the surface; preserve whether it is downward, upward, or net.
Characteristic wave height, commonly four times the standard deviation of sea-surface elevation or approximately the mean height of the highest one-third of waves.
Wave period corresponding to the spectral frequency with the greatest wave energy.
Spectrally or statistically averaged wave period. The precise spectral moment definition must be preserved when supplied.
Wave period at the peak of the wave energy spectrum.
Mean direction from which wave energy propagates, normally measured clockwise from true north.
Significant wave height of the wind-sea partition generated by local winds.
Representative period of the locally generated wind-wave partition.
Direction from which the wind-wave partition propagates.
Significant wave height of the primary swell partition, generally the swell partition with the greatest energy.
Representative period of the primary swell partition.
Direction from which the primary swell partition propagates.
Significant wave height of the secondary swell partition.
Representative period of the secondary swell partition.
Direction from which the secondary swell partition propagates.
Largest crest-to-trough wave height identified during the observation or analysis interval.
Largest crest elevation above the mean water level during the observation or analysis interval.
Eastward component of the wave-induced Stokes drift velocity at the ocean surface.
Northward component of the wave-induced Stokes drift velocity at the ocean surface.

canonical.Display Name: Relative sea level / tide-gauge water level
canonical.User-facing Definition: Sea-surface elevation measured relative to a local tide-gauge or station datum. Values from different stations are not directly comparable without datum information.
canonical.Required Qualifiers: station datum; datum history; quality tier

canonical.User-facing Definition: Height of the sea surface relative to a geodetic reference surface. In satellite altimetry it is commonly relative to a reference ellipsoid; model products may use a geoid-based reference.
Variable component of sea-surface height relative to a mean sea surface or other specified mean reference field.
Sea-surface height relative to the geoid, representing the sum of mean dynamic topography and sea-level anomaly.
Time-mean sea-surface height above the geoid associated with the mean ocean circulation.
Time-averaged sea-surface height relative to the reference ellipsoid, usually derived from long altimeter records.
Water-column height inferred from bottom pressure by a DART/tsunameter system; used to detect tsunami-related sea-level changes.
canonical.Required Qualifiers: bottom pressure; station depth; event mode

canonical.User-facing Definition: Amount of molecular oxygen dissolved in seawater, expressed as concentration per mass or volume of seawater.
Dissolved oxygen expressed relative to the equilibrium saturation concentration at the observed temperature, salinity, and pressure.
Concentration of nitrate (NO3−) in seawater.
Concentration of nitrite (NO2−) in seawater.
Combined concentration of nitrate and nitrite. It must not be treated as pure nitrate unless the source documents nitrite as negligible or separately resolved.
Concentration of dissolved phosphate in seawater.
Concentration of dissolved silicate in seawater.
Concentration of dissolved ammonium in seawater.
Measure of hydrogen-ion activity on a specified pH scale. pH values are only comparable when the scale, temperature and pressure/reference conditions are retained.
Total concentration of dissolved inorganic carbon species in seawater: dissolved CO2, bicarbonate, and carbonate.
Acid-neutralizing capacity of seawater, commonly expressed as micromoles of charge per kilogram.
Fugacity of carbon dioxide in seawater, a pressure-like quantity corrected for non-ideal gas behaviour.
Partial pressure of carbon dioxide in equilibrium with seawater. It differs slightly from CO2 fugacity because of gas non-ideality.
Mole fraction of carbon dioxide in the gas phase, commonly measured in equilibrator headspace or atmosphere.
Concentration of chlorophyll-a pigment in water, measured directly or estimated from calibrated optical/satellite algorithms.
Optical fluorescence signal associated with chlorophyll. It is a sensor signal or derived estimate and is not automatically equivalent to pigment concentration.
canonical.Canonical / Typical Unit: source unit / mg m-3 if calibrated

canonical.User-facing Definition: Fluorescence signal from coloured dissolved organic matter (CDOM), used as an optical proxy for dissolved organic material.
Backscattering coefficient due to particles in seawater at a stated wavelength.
Total optical backscattering coefficient of seawater, including water and particulate contributions.
Ratio of water-leaving radiance to downwelling irradiance just above the water surface at a specified wavelength.
Radiant flux incident on a horizontal surface from the upper hemisphere at a specified wavelength.
Photon irradiance integrated over the photosynthetically active spectral range, approximately 400–700 nm.
Exponential attenuation rate of downwelling irradiance with depth, usually specified for a wavelength or for PAR.
Mass concentration of suspended particulate material in water.
A documented observation or sampling record indicating that a taxon was detected or evaluated at a place and time.
Number of individual organisms represented by an occurrence or sample.
Amount of organisms represented by a record using a stated quantity type, such as count, percent cover, biomass, or concentration.
Mass of biological material for a taxon, community, or sample, normalized by area, volume, or sample as documented.
Statement of whether a taxon was detected (present) or not detected (absent) in a sampling event.
Fraction or percentage of a grid cell or observed area covered by sea ice.
Categorical classification describing open water, open ice, closed ice, or an ice-edge state according to the product definition.
Categorical classification of ice age/type, commonly first-year ice versus multiyear ice.
Eastward component of sea-ice displacement or drift velocity over a stated time interval.
Northward component of sea-ice displacement or drift velocity over a stated time interval.
Vertical thickness of the sea-ice layer, with product-specific definition for whether open water is included in area averaging.
Height of the ice or snow-ice interface above the local sea surface, depending on the retrieval definition.

doNotMerge.Examples: TEMP / WTMP / SST / SSTskin / SSTsubskin / SSTfnd / THETA
doNotMerge.Rule: Do not flatten to one number type.
doNotMerge.App implementation: Show parent 'Temperature' but preserve canonical key and SST subtype/reference pressure. In-situ water temperature, surface temperature, potential temperature and GHRSST SST layers represent different physical quantities.
Group under 'Salinity'; preserve salinity scale and surface/profile context. Practical Salinity (PSS-78) is not the same quantity as TEOS-10 Absolute Salinity.
Pressure can be converted approximately to depth using latitude; sample depth is not bottom depth. Keep original vertical coordinate and vertical reference.
Normalize only after recording direction_convention: winds/waves are normally FROM, currents are normally TO.
Expose 'Wave period' parent with subtype dominant, peak, mean_m10, mean_m02, etc.

doNotMerge.Examples: WVHT / VHM0 / WWH / S1HT / S2HT / VCMX
doNotMerge.App implementation: Expose 'Wave height' parent; preserve total/wind-wave/swell partition and significant vs maximum statistic.
Map concentration products together after unit normalization; never merge oxygen saturation percentage with concentration.
Use nitrate_plus_nitrite when the source cannot distinguish nitrate from nitrate+nitrite.

doNotMerge.Rule: Same conceptual parent, not directly comparable.
doNotMerge.App implementation: One UI label 'pH' is acceptable, but require qualifiers for pH scale, reference temperature and reference pressure; warn if unknown.
Display under parent 'CO2 / carbonate system' but keep fCO2, pCO2 and xCO2 as separate canonical variables.
Do not treat raw fluorescence as concentration. Keep measurement method/algorithm; calibrated concentration can map to chlorophyll-a.
Keep particulate and total backscatter separate; extract wavelength as metadata.
Use one canonical variable per physical quantity with wavelength_nm, rather than hundreds of wavelength-specific UI names.

doNotMerge.Examples: tide-gauge sea_level / SSH / SLA / ADT / MDT / MSS
doNotMerge.App implementation: Use a Sea Level parent group but do not merge; preserve datum/geoid/ellipsoid/mean field and processing level.
L2P can represent observation-level satellite retrievals; L4 is gap-filled analysis. Mark processing level so the app does not count L4 cells as independent observations.
DCDB soundings are measurements. GEBCO is a gridded synthesis containing measured and inferred sources; keep product class/provenance.
Use individual count only for counts. organismQuantity requires organismQuantityType and unit; biomass needs wet/dry/carbon basis and normalization.

doNotMerge.Examples: concentration / edge / type / drift / thickness / freeboard
doNotMerge.App implementation: Group under Sea Ice but keep separate canonical variables; preserve algorithm/product and interval for drift.
